overall: The AG found the Board violated the Open Meeting Law by discussing budget-balancing matters in executive session under Purpose 3 at its April 29 meeting, and flagged, unprompted, a missing roll-call vote and inaccurate minutes.

allegations.summary: Complainants allege the Board discussed matters not appropriate for executive session at its April 29 meeting, where it had invoked Purpose 3 (collective bargaining).
allegations.key_passage: Rather, the Board’s discussions pertained to methods and tools it would use to balance the budget and as such were related more to general budgetary matters.

allegations.summary: Not raised in the complaints: the AG noted from the video that the Board never voted by roll call to enter executive session, only a motion and second.
allegations.key_passage: After watching a video recording of the April 29 meeting, the Board did not vote to convene in executive session.

allegations.summary: Not raised in the complaints: the AG noted the April 29 minutes record a unanimous roll call vote to enter executive session that did not actually occur.
allegations.key_passage: Because the minutes must accurately capture the discussions and actions that actually took place, it is inappropriate to include information in meeting minutes that was not discussed or did not occur at a meeting.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law's requirements.
Within 30 days of the letter, release the April 29 executive session minutes in their entirety, with no redaction or withholding, and notify the AG's office that it has done so.
remedy_passage: We order immediate and future compliance with the law’s requirements, and we caution that similar future violations could be considered evidence of intent to violate the law. In addition, we order the Board, within 30 days of the date of this letter, to release the executive session minutes of the meeting held on April 29 in their entirety and to notify our office that it has done so.
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
